answered.sql: SELECT pm.name, m.metric_name, m.value FROM Metrics m JOIN Product_Managers_Metrics pmm ON m.id = pmm.metrics_id JOIN Product_Managers pm ON pmm.product_manager_id = pm.id WHERE m.id IN (SELECT metrics_id FROM Product_Managers_Metrics GROUP BY metrics_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT product_manager_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Product_Managers))

candidates.meaning: Show metrics associated with each product manager by joining the tables and grouping by product manager name.
candidates.sql: SELECT pm.name, m.metric_name, m.value FROM Product_Managers pm JOIN Product_Managers_Metrics pmm ON pm.id = pmm.product_manager_id JOIN Metrics m ON pmm.metrics_id = m.id

candidates.meaning: Show the metrics associated with each product manager by joining the Product_Managers and Product_Managers_Metrics tables to get the metrics IDs and then joining with the Metrics table to get the metric names and values.
candidates.sql: SELECT PM.name, M.metric_name, M.value FROM Product_Managers PM JOIN Product_Managers_Metrics PMM ON PM.id = PMM.product_manager_id JOIN Metrics M ON PMM.metrics_id = M.id

candidates.meaning: Display the metrics associated with each product manager, showing the metric name and value for each product manager, even if they have no metrics associated.
candidates.sql: SELECT PM.name, M.metric_name, M.value FROM Product_Managers PM LEFT JOIN Product_Managers_Metrics PMM ON PM.id = PMM.product_manager_id LEFT JOIN Metrics M ON PMM.metrics_id = M.id

candidates.meaning: List the metrics associated with each product manager, showing the metric name and value, but only for metrics that are associated with at least two product managers.
candidates.sql: SELECT PM.name, M.metric_name, M.value FROM Product_Managers PM JOIN Product_Managers_Metrics PMM ON PM.id = PMM.product_manager_id JOIN Metrics M ON PMM.metrics_id = M.id GROUP BY PM.id, M.metric_name, M.value HAVING COUNT(PMM.metrics_id) >= 2
